# hedera_cross_campus_challenge_submission_guidelines.pdf (3 pages)


## Page 1

Hedera Cross Campus Challenge 2026 - Submission Guidelines
Page 1
 HEDERA CROSS CAMPUS CHALLENGE 2026
 Hackathon Submission Guidelines
Your objective: identify a relevant problem, build a working Proof of Concept, demonstrate a meaningful use of
Hedera, and clearly explain the potential of your solution.
The goal is not to build a production-ready product or a complete MVP. A simple but functional Proof of Concept (PoC)
that demonstrates the core idea and its technical feasibility is enough.
1. 4Hacks registration is mandatory
All participants must be registered on 4Hacks and join the Campus Edition corresponding to their university or campus.
On 4Hacks, you can find the different Campus Editions. Simply choose the edition for your campus. 4Hacks is the official
platform used for:
  Participant registration
  Team creation and team formation
  Project submission
  Challenge thematic areas and information
  Submission requirements and Campus Edition details
 Project submission and team formation are managed directly through 4Hacks, so registration is mandatory for
all participants.
2. Project submission on 4Hacks
Each team must submit its project through the 4Hacks page of its Campus Edition before the announced submission
deadline.
Once you are registered, logged in, and have joined your Campus Edition, you will have access to the Submit Project
button. Clicking it opens the official submission form.
The form clearly indicates which fields are required and which are optional. It may request project information, the
problem and solution, Hedera integration, a GitHub/source-code repository, demo links, pitch materials, and other
relevant details.
 The 4Hacks submission form is the source of truth for the exact required and optional fields.
3. Submit early - you can edit until the deadline
You do not need to wait until hackathon day to create your project submission. We strongly recommend submitting
early.
Your project submission can be edited and updated as many times as needed before the final submission
deadline. The judges will evaluate the latest version available on 4Hacks when the deadline is reached.
  Complete all mandatory fields
  Keep project information up to date
  Make sure repository and submitted links are accessible
  Verify demo links work and pitch materials can be opened
 
4. What you are expected to build


## Page 2

Hedera Cross Campus Challenge 2026 - Submission Guidelines
Page 2
Build a working Proof of Concept (PoC) that demonstrates the main idea behind your solution. You are not expected to
deliver a production-ready application or complete commercial MVP.
  The core idea works
  The main functionality can be demonstrated
  The technical approach is feasible
  Hedera is genuinely integrated into the solution
 A simple, functional PoC is better than an overly ambitious project with many unfinished features. Focus on the core
functionality that best demonstrates the value of your solution.
5. Pitch presentation
Prepare a pitch of approximately 5 minutes. It may be delivered in English or French. Your presentation should
communicate both the technical side of the project and its real-world / business potential.
A deck of around 5 to 7 slides is recommended, but it is not a mandatory limit. You are free to structure and design the
presentation as you wish, provided the important elements are clear.
Slide
Suggested content
1 - Project & Team
Project name, one-line description, team members
2 - Problem
What problem are you solving, for whom, and why does it matter?
3 - Solution
What does your solution do and how does it address the problem?
4 - Product / PoC
Show the user flow, main functionality, or working demonstration
5 - Technology & Hedera
Architecture, how Hedera is integrated, and why it is useful
6 - Impact & Adoption
Who could use it, value created, and adoption potential
7 - Conclusion / Vision
Why it matters, what is different, and what could come next
This is only an example. What matters is that the judges clearly understand your Problem -> Solution -> Product -> Hedera
Integration -> Potential Impact.
6. Product demonstration
Whenever possible, demonstrate your working Proof of Concept rather than relying only on presentation slides. The
prototype does not need to be polished or production-ready.
  What the user is seeing
  What functionality is working
  Where Hedera is involved
  What your team implemented
  What could be developed further after the hackathon
 A short and reliable demonstration is usually better than showing too many unfinished features.
7. Judging criteria
 Criterion
Weight
Problem relevance and clarity
15%
Meaningful Hedera integration
25%
Technical execution and functionality
20%
Innovation and differentiation
15%
Real-world impact and adoption potential
15%
Pitch and product demonstration
10%


## Page 3

Hedera Cross Campus Challenge 2026 - Submission Guidelines
Page 3
Because Meaningful Hedera Integration represents 25% of the final evaluation, teams should be able to clearly
answer: Why does this solution use Hedera?
The judges should understand what Hedera enables, improves, or makes possible within the project. Teams are free to
use the Hedera services and technologies most appropriate for their solution.
8. Hackathon day information
Dates, start and end times, submission deadlines, physical location, online/in-person format, presentation schedule, and
Campus-specific instructions may vary between Campus Editions.
Participants will receive the relevant information through Dar Blockchain communications, their Campus / University
communication channels, and their official 4Hacks Campus Edition page.
9. Final checklist
■ Registered on 4Hacks
■ Joined the correct Campus Edition
■ Created or joined a team on 4Hacks
■ Reviewed the challenge thematic areas and information
■ Opened Submit Project and reviewed the required fields
■ Created the project submission early
■ Completed all mandatory fields before the deadline
■ Prepared a working Proof of Concept
■ Prepared the pitch deck and approximately 5-minute pitch
■ Prepared the product demonstration
■ Verified that all submitted links are accessible
■ Updated the submission with the latest version before the deadline
 Build something useful. Make it work. Show us why Hedera matters.
 
Good luck to all teams participating in the Hedera Cross Campus Challenge 2026.
